questions.text: James Smith, a CFA candidate, serves on the board of a publicly traded firm, NovaTech. During a closed board meeting, James Smith learns that NovaTech will surprisingly slash its dividend by 50% next week. However, James Smith realizes this cut indicates severe industry-wide macroeconomic stress and aggressively short-sells a highly correlated competitor, Quantum Materials. According to the CFA Institute Standards, James Smith:
options: Did not violate the standards because {competitor} was not the subject of the inside information and mosaic theory applies.
Violated the standards by trading {competitor} because the information was material, non-public, and affected the entire sector.
Violated the standards because board members are strictly prohibited from trading any stocks in the same sector.
questions.hint: Material nonpublic information (MNPI) applies to any security whose price would be significantly impacted by the information, even if it's not the specific company the information originated from.
questions.explanation: Standard II(A) Material Nonpublic Information prohibits trading on MNPI. If the dividend cut of a major firm is highly material to a correlated competitor, trading the competitor's stock based on that closed-door information is a violation. It does not qualify as mosaic theory because the foundational piece of information is explicitly non-public and material.

questions.text: A portfolio manager wants to test whether the mean monthly return of a newly formed quantitative strategy exceeds 0.5%. options: t-statistic: 0.83; Fail to reject the null hypothesis
t-statistic: 1.00; Fail to reject the null hypothesis
questions.hint: Use the t-statistic formula: (Sample Mean - Target Mean) / (Sample Std Dev / sqrt(n)). Remember this is a one-tailed test.
